Claim: H1: days after more upwind fire detections have higher PM2.5
Data used: 4,757 treated winter station-days from 39 stations on 129 dates
Method: log PM2.5 on the previous day's upwind fire count (100 km, 45 degrees) with weather controls, station and weekday effects; date and station clustered intervals
How far to trust it: Low: the interval includes zero under 4 other ways of building it, and the placebo gives 41% of the main effect

Claim: H2: PM2.5 is lower after a GRAP stage is activated than weather and fires alone predict
Data used: 30 stage changes, 1 primary event, treated stations with control cities as comparison
Method: counterfactual from weather and upwind fire on the 60 days before the change, a hold-out check, placebo dates and control cities
Main result with interval: -21.7% over days 1 to 3 for the primary event (interval -39.8% to +1.3%), not usable
How far to trust it: None: 0 of 5 events pass the hold-out check
